gaps.property: Property 2 (falsifiable) — and the standard's explicit check for conflict with another module's ownership
gaps.problem: Head-on ownership inversion with the sibling spec, which makes item 6's integrated branch unbuildable. traffic.md:25 says "**`props` owns the signal phase clock; traffic reads it**" and traffic.md:165 makes traffic's signalState()/signals() read-through wrappers over props.signalFor(). props.md:40-41 says the exact opposite — "props renders the heads, traffic decides the phase… `traffic` owns the signal state machine (traffic.md §2); this spec does not contest that" — and props.md:101 defines signalFor as a "pure read-through of ctx.modules.traffic.signalState(nodeId) whenever traffic is present". In `?showcase=all` both functions exist, so traffic.signalState → props.signalFor → traffic.signalState is infinite recursion; if either builder guards it, there is no clock at all. This is not theoretical: props.md item 10(b) grades props by injecting a stub `ctx.modules.traffic = {signalState: ...}` and requiring `source === 'traffic'` within one frame, so the props builder is contractually forced into the read-through direction. Worse, props.md:556-559 books this very failure ("Two clocks for one signal… An earlier draft of this spec and traffic.md both claimed to own the signal phase") and declares it settled in the direction traffic.md now reverses. Item 6's integrated probe ("greenArms agrees 100 % with the arms props reports green") is then vacuous — two mirrors of each other always agree — while the actual behaviour is a stack overflow. The supporting citations are also wrong: traffic.md:26 cites "props.md (lines 31-32, 74-75)" for the signalFor freeze (those lines are world.props ownership prose and LOD prose; the signature is at props.md:98-101), :33-35 for the phase-clock resolution (that is showcase-staging prose), and §7 cites "props.md:11, :384" for props' dependencies (actually :20 and :570). A builder who follows the citations reads the wrong paragraphs and never sees the inversion.
gaps.fix: Flip traffic.md to match the already-frozen direction: traffic owns the phase state machine, props renders the heads and mirrors it. Rewrite the preamble bullet at :25-40, the §2 paragraph at :165-171 (signalState/signals become the authoritative source, not wrappers), item 6's integrated branch (grade that props' lenses follow traffic's greenArms, and that no vehicle crosses a red — not that two read-throughs agree), item 22 (masts disappear when props publishes a trafficlight item — that part already works either way), and the two `props` rows in §7's dependency block and degradation table. Delete the claim that traffic "never owns the phase where props is live", and fix the four citations to props.md:40-51 and :98-101. If instead the intent really is props-owns, then props.md must be edited in the same commit — but do not ship the pair as they stand.

gaps.property: Property 1 (sequenced) — "state what must exist before the work starts"
gaps.problem: "`src/modules/traffic/index.js` is still the stub" (traffic.md:9) is false. The working tree holds a 2 078-line implementation — index.js 244 lines (modified), plus untracked geometry.js 598, sim.js 633, graph.js 301, materials.js 265, showcase.js 37 — all timestamped today, 15:02-15:09. Only the 14-line stub is committed, and STATUS.json still says `"traffic": {round: 0, status: "stub"}`, so the spec matches the bookkeeping and contradicts the disk. BUILDER.md step 6 tells the builder to read "your own folder as it stands", so they will hit it immediately and have to guess: extend or rewrite? The existing API is incompatible with §2 in ways that decide that guess — `lightState(nodeId)` not `signalState`, `flowGrid()` returning `{size, cellSize, data, sample(x,z)}` instead of the named-Float32Array + `index`/`sample(name,x,z)` shape, `spawnVehicle` returning `null` instead of `-1`, `kinds()` as a function instead of `world.traffic.kinds`, extra `setTargets`/`preroll`/`_debug`, and no setDensity/density/step/freeze/forceLod/vehicle/debug at all; and `dependencies: ['roads']` with `budget: {drawCalls: 90, triangles: 520_000}` against the spec's `['terrain','roads','simulation']` and `{60, 300_000}`. Two competent builders will not make the same call here, and the one who extends inherits a `sim.js` that steps agents from `dt * clock speed` (index.js:100-101, `const sdt = Math.min(0.1, dt) * speed`) — which is failure mode §6(a), the dead fleet at speed 0, already in the building.
gaps.fix: Replace the "still the stub" sentence with the real state and an explicit disposition: name the six files and their line counts, say whether they are prior exploratory work to be deleted and rebuilt or a starting point to be brought up to §2, and list the breaking renames the builder must make either way (lightState→signalState, flowGrid shape, spawnVehicle return, kinds()→world.traffic.kinds, dependencies, budget). Add one line pointing at index.js:100-101 as an instance of §6's dead-fleet mode so it is not re-shipped.

gaps.property: Property 2 (falsifiable) — plus the standard's rule that role-file content is not restated in a module spec
gaps.problem: Eight named grading shots are never produced by the matrix the critic actually runs, so the items that depend on them cannot be graded without an argument about who was supposed to shoot what. CRITIC.md's command is `gauntlet --times 12,22` (8 shots) plus two hand-shot golden-hour frames (skyline_17p5, street_6p5) plus each declared preset once, night presets at 22 — and STATUS.json's throughput note confirms the matrix was deliberately reduced because SwiftShader needs 3-10 s per frame. But item 1 grades at `junction_12`, `queue_12`, `crossing_6p5`, `merge_12`; item 5 at `queue_17p5`; item 6 at `junction_12` and `junction_22`; item 9 at `crossing_12` and `crossing_6p5`; item 10 at `closeup_17p5` and `junction_6p5`; item 2 at `fleet_12`. None of `junction_6p5`, `junction_22`, `queue_12`, `queue_17p5`, `crossing_6p5`, `crossing_12`, `closeup_17p5` falls out of the default run. §8 compounds this by asserting its own matrix — "Critics shoot aerial, street, skyline, closeup × 6.5, 12, 17.5, 22" — which is the 16-shot gauntlet that CRITIC.md no longer runs. That is duplicated role-file content that has already drifted, exactly what the standard warns about.
gaps.fix: Delete the shot-matrix sentence from §8 (it belongs to CRITIC.md and is now stale) and replace it with an explicit "extra captures this module needs" block giving the literal commands for the preset×time combinations the acceptance items name — junction at 6.5/12/22, queue at 12/17.5, crossing at 6.5/12, closeup at 17.5, merge and fleet at 12 — or retarget those items onto shots the default matrix produces. Roughly ten extra frames at 3-10 s each is affordable; the ambiguity is not.

gaps.problem: Item 21's determinism check is ambiguous in a way its own preamble proves is load-bearing. It requires "identical `x, z, heading` (to 1e-4) for the first 20 vehicle ids". §2 says ids are unique for the session and never reused after despawn, and the item's own opening concedes that the number of steps — hence spawns and despawns — before `__sim.ready` depends on machine load. So by the time the probe runs its pin sequence (freeze → setDensity(0) → step(60) → setDensity(null) → step(1) → step(600)), the id counter has reached a different value in run A than in run B: the re-seeded fleet might be ids 431-450 in one and 587-606 in the other. Read as "ids 1-20" the item can never pass; read as "the first 20 entries of the Map in insertion order" it passes cleanly. The builder will implement one reading and the critic will probe the other. Relatedly, `ctx.rng.fork(label)` (core/rng.js:64) is `new RNG(this.seed, label)` — keyed on seed and label only, with no notion of sequence position — so the item's phrase "re-fork the module rng from a fixed sequence position" describes an API that does not work that way, and the requirement that the re-seeded fleet be a pure function of seed *and* `world.time.hour` has no stated mechanism for the hour to enter the stream.
gaps.fix: Say "the first 20 entries of `world.traffic.vehicles` in insertion order" and drop "ids". Replace "from a fixed sequence position" with the real contract: "`ctx.rng.fork('traffic:fleet')` is keyed on `world.seed` and the label alone (core/rng.js:64), so re-forking always yields the same stream; fold the hour in explicitly, e.g. `fork('traffic:fleet:' + hour.toFixed(2))`, if the seeded fleet is to differ by hour."

gaps.problem: `$REF` is hardcoded at traffic.md:7 to `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-SimBuild/c06ed41b-9bdf-5ab7-ace6-40b62a5e4281/scratchpad/ref/` with no fallback. The sibling spec explicitly documents that this path "does **not** survive into a new session" (props.md:9-11) and gives a three-step resolution chain plus a clause saying that if the frames cannot be resolved, §3's prose descriptions are the bar. traffic.md has neither. The directory happens to exist right now, so this fails silently later rather than now: a builder resumed in a fresh session finds nothing at that path, and §3's entire visual target — which is anchored to cs2_5 for model quality, cs2_1 for behaviour, cs2_8 for night, cs2_4 for density — loses its anchor. §3's prose is good enough to stand in, but nothing in the spec says so.
gaps.fix: Copy props.md:9-14 verbatim: `$SIMBUILD_REF` → `~/.simbuild/ref/` → the session scratchpad path, the note that the frames are never committed (ARCHITECTURE §10) and are re-fetchable from the Steam URLs recorded with docs/reference/CS2-LOOK.md, and the fallback clause that §3's prose descriptions are the graded bar when the frames cannot be resolved.

gaps.problem: Three smaller under-specifications, each of which is a probe that can be implemented two ways. (a) `freeze(v)` is defined in §2 as "true: `update()` stops stepping agents", but items 12 and 21 both do `api.freeze(true)` and then `api.step(n)` and expect the agents to advance — nothing says step() bypasses freeze, and a builder who implements step() to respect freeze makes both items unprobeable. (b) Item 7's ceiling probe is `max(stats().emissive.head, .tail, .brake) < 6.5 <= stats().emissive.mast`, but item 22 requires `stats().emissive.mast` to be `null` under `?showcase=all`; the comparison against null is false, so the probe fails in the integrated shots on a module that is behaving correctly. (c) `stats().tris` carries the ≤ 300 000 cap, but the spec never says whether it counts rendered triangles or authored source geometry — the setDensity(0) delta row implies rendered, while `byKindTris` ("LOD0 triangles of one instance") implies authored, and at 240 vehicles × ~1 000 + 260 pedestrians × 320 the authored reading blows the cap while the rendered reading passes comfortably.
gaps.fix: Three sentences. In §2 under `step`: "advances agents even while `freeze(true)` is held; `freeze` only stops `update()` from stepping." In item 7: "where no mast is drawn (`stats().emissive.mast === null`, i.e. `?showcase=all`), the ceiling is the literal 6.5 and the mast comparison is skipped." In §5: "`stats().tris` is triangles actually submitted this frame after LOD and culling, not authored source geometry."

strengths: Dependency APIs are real and were spot-checked line by line: roads types table (alley 8/1/30/2/2.0/4/3.6, street 16/2/50/3/5.0/6/3.8, avenue 24/4/60/4/8.0, highway 32/6/100/0/16.0/10/3.8/1.9/2.4) is copied verbatim from network.js:6-11; ROAD_LIFT=0.08 at build.js:12 and SW_H=0.16 at build.js:18 give exactly the 0.21 m sidewalk top the spec states; laneOffsets' per=max(1,floor(lanes/2)) sign convention in item 4 matches network.js:210-225 exactly; intersections() really does carry stopT/atA/lanesIn/ring (build.js:1231-1243); laneCenter returns null for an unknown edge (network.js:228-230); ui/hud.js:796 really reads world.traffic.vehicles.get(id); simulation/index.js:187 step(n); core/debug.js:24 heapMB. Almost nothing here is invented.

The world.traffic block in §2 is a character-for-character copy of ARCHITECTURE §3, and the pedestrian record — left as `{...}` in the architecture — is fixed here with a full field contract rather than paraphrased.

The bloom-threshold chain is derived, not asserted: environment/index.js:186 sets exposure 2.8 at night, effects/index.js:140 sets thr = lerp(2.6,2.2,night)/exposure, giving 0.79 — the same 0.79 effects_r1 issue 2 measured — and item 7's radiance bands (head 3.0-5.0, tail 1.2-2.0, brake 3.5-5.0, mast 6.5-9.0) all sit in a defensible relation to it. The "nothing brighter than the signal lens" prose is made a consequence of the numbers instead of a competing claim.

§6 is sixteen real, project-sourced failure modes with verifiable citations, not generic advice: roads_r1's "Terrain protrudes through the carriageway (−0.44 m)", effects_r1's "Night is a milky blue dusk", roads_r1's "White speckle/sparkle across asphalt", simulation_r1 issue 6's non-repeatable screenshots, environment_r2's milky 17:30, ui_r1's 720p overflow, simulation_r1's "Trees are lollipops" — every one checks out against docs/critic/.

The two-clocks analysis is the best thing in the spec and is correct against the code: main.js sets speed 0 when --time is passed without --speed, and passes real clamped dt to registry.update regardless, so "phase from world.time, agent motion from raw dt" is exactly what makes the gauntlet frames both repeatable and alive. The corollary — "no acceptance item may require a pixel-identical frame from two loads" — is then enforced consistently across items 11, 12 and 21.

The A/B/C/D mask protocol in the §4 preamble turns every "on vehicle surfaces" and "the shadow" phrase into a mechanical measurement, and debug.setVisible is specified in §2 so the critic can actually build the masks. Item 10's self-scaling darkening test (fractions of on-screen length L) is the right way to write a pixel criterion that survives a zoom change.

The showcase network in §8 states every endpoint, so the four outside connections land at |x| or |z| ≥ 980 against item 15's ≥ 964 border test, and the core street/closeup/night_street presets (targets [40,0,40], [20,6,20], [-40,0,60]) match core/camera.js:23-28 exactly — item 14's "must land on live traffic" is staged rather than hoped for.

Budget is consistent with ARCHITECTURE §9 and deliberately under it: 60 declared of traffic's 150 draw-call allotment, ≤ 1.6 ms against §9's ≤ 2 ms per module, and the whole-frame triangle figure is explicitly graded as a setDensity(0) delta rather than as an absolute the module cannot control — which pre-empts the exact argument roads' 1 208 995-triangle showcase would otherwise cause.
verdict:
A genuinely strong spec held below the line by one cross-module contradiction and one false premise. On the properties the standard weighs most heavily it is close to exemplary: the world-data block is copied verbatim from ARCHITECTURE §3 rather than paraphrased, the dependency APIs are real (I checked laneOffsets, intersections, laneCenter's null return, ROAD_LIFT/SW_H, the roads types table, grids.expose, hud.js:796, debug.js:24 and simulation's step(n) against the source and every one matched), the failure modes are sixteen real critic findings with quotable evidence rather than generic advice, the budget sits deliberately under ARCHITECTURE §9's 150 draw calls and 2 ms, and the two-clocks analysis correctly derives repeatable-but-alive frames from main.js's speed-0 behaviour. The §4 mask protocol turns most of the pixel language into mechanical measurement, which is rare.

It fails on the standard's own ownership check. traffic.md:25 declares props the owner of the signal phase and makes traffic's signalState a read-through of props.signalFor; props.md:40-41 and :101 declare traffic the owner and make props.signalFor a read-through of traffic.signalState. In ?showcase=all that is mutual recursion, and props.md item 10(b) already grades the props builder into its direction with a stub probe, so the props side cannot yield. props.md:556-559 books this exact failure as settled — in the direction traffic.md reverses. Item 6's integrated branch, the largest branch of the highest-value behavioural item, therefore grades two mirrors against each other while the real system deadlocks. Compounding it, every citation traffic.md offers for the freeze points at the wrong lines of props.md, so a builder who checks the references never finds the disagreement.

Second, the spec opens by telling the builder the module is a stub. It is not: 2 078 lines exist on disk, written today, with an incompatible API surface and an agent stepper that already commits §6's dead-fleet mistake. STATUS.json agrees with the spec and disagrees with the disk, so the builder discovers this at step 6 of BUILDER.md with no guidance on whether to extend or rebuild — the single largest unforced guess in the document.

Third, eight of the named grading shots are not produced by the matrix CRITIC.md actually runs, and §8 restates a 16-shot matrix that the role file abandoned for throughput reasons — duplicated role-file content that has already drifted, and five acceptance items ride on it.

Lens 1: two competent builders converge on the fleet, the materials, the LODs, the pedestrians and the night lighting — the numbers are there and they are sourced — but they diverge on the signal phase, on what to do with the existing implementation, and on freeze/step semantics. Lens 2: roughly eighteen of twenty-two items are mechanically checkable as written; items 6 (integrated), 10, 21 and parts of 1, 5 and 9 are arguments waiting to happen, mostly over missing shots and one ambiguous phrase. Fix gap 1 and gap 2 and this is a 9; gaps 3-6 are an hour of editing. As it stands, 8.0 — below the 8.5 bar, and the shortfall is concentrated in exactly the places that would cost a round.
